policy_prompt_for_subgoal: The episode starts in A (press button): the first decision step, with empty memory and no execution steps, is always A. Rules, applied to whatever situation you are in: 1. If button_pressed is `no` (or memory is empty) and no execution step in front of you shows the button pressed down: choose A, press button. 2. If the scene at this decision step (or the last execution steps) shows a cube held in the gripper (fingers ~46% open, cube marked 'is held in the gripper'): choose C, place the cube onto the table. 3. If the gripper is empty (fingers open, no cube held) and button_pressed is `yes` (or this step's execution steps showed the button pressed down) and pending_cubes (after this step's update) is non-empty: choose B, pick up the highlighted cube, pointing at the FIRST entry of pending_cubes (the list is sorted with the robot's leftmost cube, largest x, first). Point at that stored [y, x], or at the cube visible within a few pixels of it (cube positions wobble). If no cube is currently listed at that position it is merely hidden by the arm: still choose B at the stored point; never skip to a later entry and never treat the list as empty. 4. Only when the pending_cubes carried in was already empty, nothing was picked up at this step, the gripper is empty, and button_pressed is `yes`: the task is finished; choose C (place) as a harmless no-op. A step that merely shows a placing (fingers reopened, cube back on the table) with a non-empty carried list is not finished: apply rule 3 and choose B at the first carried entry. 5. Any situation not covered: if a cube is held choose C; else if any cube position is remembered in pending_cubes choose B at its first entry; else choose A.

fields.name: button_pressed
fields.description: Write `no` when the memory carried in says `no` (or is empty) and no execution step in front of you shows the button pressed down. At the first decision step, when the memory carried in is empty, write the starting value `no` explicitly; never leave the field blank. Write `yes` as soon as any execution step shown at this step says the button is pressed down, or the memory carried in already says `yes`. Never go back to `no`. e.g. yes

fields.name: pending_cubes
fields.description: Ordered list of [y, x] of cubes on highlighted white areas not yet picked up. At the first decision step (memory carried in empty, no execution steps) write `[]` explicitly; never leave it blank. When the execution steps shown at this step list `highlighted area` positions (they appear right after the button press and vanish before the decision step), write one entry per highlighted area: the [y, x] of the cube nearest that area, and sort the entries by x from largest to smallest (the robot's leftmost cube first), not in the order the areas are listed. Otherwise copy the list carried in, but if the execution steps shown at this step show a pick-up (the gripper descends onto a cube with open fingers, closes to about 46%, and that cube is then marked 'is held in the gripper'), remove the ONE entry whose stored [y, x] is nearest the position where the gripper closed (the held cube's position just before it was lifted), whatever its place in the list, and keep all other entries. Do not remove anything on a placing step, i.e. one whose first execution frame already shows a cube held and whose later frames show the fingers opening to ~88-100% and the cube resting on the table again: copy the list unchanged. Never remove an entry just because no cube is currently observed at its position; a cube can be hidden by the arm and still remain pending. Example: carried [[118, 147], [70, 152]], execution steps show the gripper closing at [118, 147] and a cube held -> write [[70, 152]]. e.g. [[89, 146], [63, 150]]
